rationale: Direct candidate-ID mapping with deterministic finite-state transitions is recommended because it introduces the minimum new semantic surface required to make the adaptive arm executable while preserving provenance, replay, isolation, and deterministic governance boundaries. The recommendation is not a human approval and was not selected using comparative performance evidence. Adaptive state may influence candidate selection only and does not acquire execution or governance authority.

selection_rule.proposed: Exclude SUPPRESSED and COMPLETED; retain UNTRIED and ELIGIBLE; search after the most recently selected candidate; wrap once; select the first valid candidate in frozen ordering.

stopping_rule: STOP_NO_ELIGIBLE_CANDIDATE; invalid transitions terminate the trajectory fail-closed; no authority or governance rule may be changed.
determinism_invariants: same state + same action + same permitted feedback = same next state
same frozen candidate space + same state + same permitted feedback = same next candidate
no inferred transition when feedback is insufficient
state is reconstructible from the append-only event sequence
selection uses no hidden state, confidence, semantic preference, or runtime ranking
